protocol_notes.paper_says: Section 5 (p. 6): 'the official validation and test sets containing 35 and 70 samples per class, respectively'. Section 3.1 (p. 3): the MultiMeDaLIS corpus of 126 classes totals 25,830 gesture instances.
protocol_notes.evidence_says: Validation: 35 per class is consistent (126 x 35 = 4,410). Test: every source has 7,560 rows, not 126 x 70 = 8,820. (1) The downloaded competition data has 4,410 val and 7,560 test sample folders (run data-populate-rules-accepted-001, INVENTORY.json). (2) Kaggle totalSolutionRows is 11,970 = 4,410 + 7,560. (3) The authors' released logits (author-logits) hold 4,410 val and 7,560 test ids. (4) Every prediction CSV in official-code at 7dd73c4, counted on 2026-11-09 with Python's csv module (header excluded), agrees: the eight *_val.csv / *_test.csv files under Final_prediction/, MSLR_radar_video/results/predictions/ and MSLR_radar_video/fusion_with_slgcnn/predictions/ hold 4,410 and 7,560 unique ids, and the three *_all.csv files hold 11,970 (= 4,410 + 7,560). MSLR_radar_video/prediction_script/alpha_vs_accuracy.csv is an alpha sweep, not a prediction file. 7,560 / 126 = 60. The val and test folders are class-agnostic with concealed labels, so true per-class counts cannot be checked. The authors' final test predictions (Final_prediction/Final_LIS_prediction_test.csv) give 58-62 per predicted class, median 60 (2 classes at 58, 8 at 59, 107 at 60, 6 at 61, 3 at 62); their final val predictions give 32-37, median 35. The test set therefore has about 60 per class, not 70. The SignEval 2025 summary (Section 4.2) states only the totals: 12,600 train, 4,410 val and 7,560 test. Section 3.1's 25,830 equals 126 x (100 + 35 + 70) = 126 x 205. The same summary section also gives 25,830 for the full corpus (each of the 126 items performed 205 times), while the released Track-2 partition totals 24,570 (126 x 195).
protocol_notes.consequence: This is a paper-text discrepancy, not a data mismatch. The data used here match the competition release and the authors' own files. Test denominators are 7,560, not 8,820; data, targets and scoring are unaffected. The paper's '70' may come from the same 205-per-item figure (205 - 100 - 35 = 70), but this is not established. Section 3.1's 25,830 is not treated as wrong, because it may describe the full corpus rather than the released partition.

Inferring one from the held-out runs (e.g. reusing the epoch at which early stopping fired) would be a behavior-changing choice whose result would be conditional evidence, not a produced target. stop_policy_enforcement.rule: Every declared ceiling is enforced mechanically, not only recorded (operator instruction 2026-11-10 after predict-full-001's GPU-hour overrun).
stop_policy_enforcement.gpu_runs: Launch the run detached, then immediately launch `guard` (scripts/modal_app.py) as its own detached app with deadline_utc = guard_deadline(start, gpus, max_wall_s, max_gpu_hours, max_cost, usd_per_gpu_hour), where gpus is the number of GPU inputs (<= MAX_GPUS 30) and the rate is the measured all-in USD per container-hour for that function's resources plus a margin: slgcn_train (L4, 4 CPU, 16 GiB) 1.15; slgcn_test and tf_predict (L4, 8 CPU, 32 GiB; measured 1.43-1.44) 1.50; other shapes from the first billing of that shape, or Modal list prices + 10% before one exists. A local backup watcher through the wrapper stops the app 10 minutes after the deadline if it is still running and alerts if the guard app stops first. Record the guard app ID, deadline, derivation and any gap in runs[].stop_policy_enforcement.
stop_policy_enforcement.cpu_runs: The function timeout bounds wall time; ceilings are declared so that timeout x hourly rate stays within the cost ceiling. If not, a guard is launched as for GPU runs.
stop_policy_enforcement.limits: The guard relies on modal 1.6.2 internals (_Client._stub AppList/AppStop, synchronize_api); recheck after a modal upgrade with a test like pf-guard-sync-001. GPU-hours and cost are bounded from above (containers x elapsed x rate), so a run can be stopped somewhat before its true ceiling, never after it. Billing reports lag 1-2 h, so they are used for accounting, not enforcement.
stop_policy_enforcement.history: Before 2026-11-10 ceilings were enforced only through function timeouts (wall time), which did not bound GPU-hours or cost; predict-full-001 exceeded its GPU-hour ceiling (3.27 of 2.0).
stop_policy_enforcement.container_count: From slgcn-retrain-full-002 (2026-11-10) the guard is also launched with --max-tasks set to the planned container count (GPU inputs + orchestrator, e.g. 16), and stops the app when two consecutive polls see more running tasks. The deadline bounds GPU-hours and cost only while at most `gpus` GPU containers run; slgcn-retrain-full-001 showed that Modal retries preempted inputs on its own, so this premise is now enforced rather than assumed (test pf-guard-tasks-001). Orchestrators that fan out GPU work (slgcn_all) run nonpreemptible so a preemption cannot relaunch inputs that are still running.
stop_policy_enforcement.launcher: Run and guard are launched together by one local launcher script (scratchpad, not committed): modal run --detach <run>, read the new app id from the client output, compute the deadline from the launch time, modal run --detach guard, then the backup loop. The guard's first poll came 11 s after launch for slgcn-retrain-full-002. Its backup loop treats an app that drops out of `app list` after having been listed as finished (slgcn-retrain-full-002's backup kept re-issuing harmless stops to an unlisted, already-stopped app).

author-slgcn-weights-check-001: the authors' released checkpoints reproduce their released logits under these configs (100% argmax agreement); compare-slgcn-author-001: their bone stream agrees with their joint stream on 99.16%. Their bone models were therefore trained for is_vector False inputs.

dead_ends.classification: Dead end, not an ambiguity: the inference contradicted published evidence (operator, 2026-11-10).
dead_ends.attribution: The SL-GCN training configuration, including is_vector True for bone, joint-motion and bone-motion, was inferred by the reproduction agent (claude-opus-5-5-claude-code) from SAM-SLR's original training configs. The authors' published fold configs contained a train_feeder_args section with is_vector False for all four streams, which the agent did not surface. Protocol option A1, as presented to the human reproducer, described the training config only as "SAM-SLR train config" and did not disclose this contradicting evidence; the human approval of A1 was given on that basis. The inference was the agent's, not the human reproducer's.
dead_ends.why_the_section_was_discounted: The session record shows no explicit assessment of that section. The agent described official-code as having "no training configs" (gate protocol-training-recipe) and treated the fold configs as test-phase files (phase: test) whose training-related fields are not authoritative. Several of those fields do contradict the released checkpoints (num_epoch 100 and step [50] against weights paths sign_*_fold*_250/epoch-176..249), but the record does not show that this conflict was weighed at the time. The agent read only the joint fold config, where is_vector is False in both sources, and did not diff the bone, jm and bm configs field by field until 2026-11-09 after the bone stream failed.
dead_ends.what_should_have_happened: The conflict between the authors' fold configs (is_vector False) and SAM-SLR's train configs (is_vector True) should have been raised as an alternative at protocol gate protocol-training-recipe before the full run.
dead_ends.kept_or_reverted: Reverted for target results: the is_vector True models stay as retained runs and as conditional evidence (option V1: slgcn-isvector-check-001, slgcn-v1-test-001) but produce no target. Bone, jm and bm were retrained with is_vector False under gate slgcn-retrain-settings (R1, 2026-11-10) in slgcn-retrain-full-001/002, and those models produce the targets.
